# Stutter Guard - SHA-256 checksums
#
# THE AUTHORITY FOR A DOWNLOAD IS THE .sha256 ATTACHED TO ITS RELEASE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every release carries StutterGuard.exe.sha256, generated by the build job from the exact bytes it
# uploaded. Verify a download against that file:
#
#   certutil -hashfile StutterGuard.exe SHA256
#
# A file in this repository cannot describe a future release. The build job runs .NET SDK 10.0.x on a
# GitHub runner, not in my working copy, so its bytes are not mine to predict - which is the whole reason
# the checksum moved onto the release. Nothing below claims otherwise.
#
# ---- Hashes of released assets (historical record only) ----
01752CF8BCFAF8346516CFAC14DA0E1D2B468EBAACCC0923F0BAFBF39BC25B89  StutterGuard.exe  (v1.2.0)
# v1.3.0 and later: see the .sha256 file attached to the release.
#
# ---- Reproducibility, measured on a local toolchain ----
#
# Builds are reproducible in a fixed environment. Measured 2026-11-15 on .NET SDK 10.0.402, win-x64:
# two clean publishes of one commit, into two different directories, produced the same 65,446,991 bytes
# with SHA-256 E36FE73D9E6F4DEDC5D41FDD6215DC05776BC3F2D1C0809B7FD6054F6B1D5122. `build.cmd --verify-repro`
# repeats that on any machine.
#
# Scoped deliberately: a CLEAN build is reproducible against another CLEAN build. An incremental build of
# the same source differs (measured: 65,446,984 bytes), a different SDK patch level differs, and a
# different output path can differ. Reproducibility means one source tree and one toolchain give one
# artifact - not that a released binary is the same as a build of your own.
